newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent steady, EU-Iran worries ease further.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent steady, EU-Iran worries ease further.

text.p: SIMEX Brent prices were steady but untraded in Asia at noon on Monday, looking to NYMEX for direction after the EU-Iran row faded to the background.
May Brent on SIMEX was quoted at a wide $17.80/$18.15 per barrel, around the London Brent close on Friday of $17.88.
Brokers said there was little to offer fresh direction.
Tensions between Iran and the European Union, after EU countries withdrew diplomats from Tehran over the killing of Kurdish dissidents in Bonn, began to fade Friday, they said.

Market worries were further soothed over the weekend, when German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel was reported saying Bonn did not want the row to escalate, but it would later need a new evaluation of relations with Iran.
NYMEX crude on ACCESS, was last traded at $19.62 per barrel, up nine cents from New York. Volume was a modest 309 lots.
